source_text:
Διὰ τοῦτο μύρον ἔλαβεν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος, ἵνα πνέῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀφθαρσίαν, μὴ ἀλείφεσθε δυσωδίαν τῆς διδασκαλίας τοῦ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, μὴ αἰχμαλωτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ προκειμένου ζῆν.
διὰ τί δὲ οὐ πάντες φρόνιμοι γινόμεθα λαβόντες θεοῦ γνῶσιν, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός; τί μωρῶς ἀπολλύμεθα, ἀγνοοῦντες τὸ χάρισμα, ὃ πέπομφεν ἀληθῶς ὁ κύριος;
thought_title: The Lord's ointment and the gift of knowledge
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Ephesians against false teachers who corrupt faith, and now explains why the Lord received ointment on his head and why believers should accept the knowledge of God.
pass_a_gloss: Because of this ointment he received upon the head of him the Lord, in order that he might breathe to the church incorruption. Do not anoint yourselves [with] the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age, lest he take you captive from the life set before [you]. But why do not all [of us] become wise, having received knowledge of God, which is Jesus Christ? Why do we perish foolishly, ignoring the gift, which truly the Lord has sent?

choices.why: Keeps the concrete sense of perfumed oil, matching the anointing imagery in the passage.
Preserves the metaphor of the Lord exhaling a life-giving fragrance onto the church.
Matches the abstract noun and the contrast with the stench of false teaching.
Strong, concrete word that contrasts sharply with the ointment's fragrance.
Renders the articular infinitive with the participle literally, preserving the sense of the life laid out ahead.
rejected: from the life that lies before you

choices.why: Keeps the standard rendering of the term for a divine gift, here identified with knowledge of God in Christ.

pass_b_english: This is why the Lord received anointing on his head: so that he might breathe incorruption into the church. Do not anoint yourselves with the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age, lest he take you captive from the life set before you.
Why do we not all become wise, since we have received the knowledge of God, which is Jesus Christ? Why do we perish foolishly, failing to recognize the gift that the Lord has truly sent?

problems.quote: the stench of the ruler of this age's teaching
problems.why: Awkward genitive; 'ruler of this age's teaching' may misparse as ruler's teaching, not teaching that stinks.
problems.fix: Revise to 'the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age'.

problems.quote: the stench of the ruler of this age's teaching
problems.why: Possessive chain is awkward; reader may parse 'this age's teaching' as a unit rather than 'ruler of this age.'
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age.'

edits.old: the stench of the ruler of this age's teaching
edits.new: the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age

problems.quote: The Lord received ointment on his head for this reason: so that he might breathe incorruption upon the church.
problems.why: 'Breathe incorruption' reads like a literal gloss; the metaphor is unclear.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'so that he might impart incorruption to the church.'

edits.old: so that he might breathe incorruption upon the church
edits.new: so that he might impart incorruption to the church

problems.quote: the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age
problems.why: 'Stench' for teaching is odd; may be 'smell/perfume' contrast with ointment.
problems.fix: Check Greek; may mean 'evil odor' or 'corrupting influence'.

edits.old: the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age
edits.new: the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age

problems.why: 'Ruler of this age' is a demonic title; 'kingdoms of this age' refers to political powers—different concepts, but 'this age' overlap may confuse.
problems.fix: Not a drift issue; keep distinct but ensure 'ruler' is glossed as demonic.

problems.quote: Do not anoint yourselves with the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age
problems.why: Preceding sentence about Lord's ointment makes this seem like Scripture, but it is Ignatius's exhortation.
problems.fix: Clarify this is author's application, not citation.

problems.quote: the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age
problems.why: 'Foul odor' contrasts with ointment, but 'teaching' having odor is odd personification.
problems.fix: Acceptable as metaphor; or 'the stench of the ruler's teaching.'

problems.quote: This is why the Lord received ointment on his head
problems.why: 'Ointment' sounds medicinal; the reference is to anointing (funeral anointing or messianic anointing).

edits.old: This is why the Lord received ointment on his head
edits.new: This is why the Lord received anointing on his head

fixed: The glossary already specifies 'ruler of this age' as the devil, so no change is needed.
The sentence is clearly Ignatius's own exhortation following the scriptural reference; no change is needed.
The metaphor of teaching having an odor is acceptable and consistent with the ointment imagery; no change is needed.
The source μύρον refers to anointing oil or perfume, not medicinal ointment; changed 'ointment' to 'anointing' to reflect the anointing context.

problems.quote: the teaching of the ruler of this age
problems.why: 'Ruler of this age' is Satan, but 'teaching of the ruler of this age' is odd—Satan doesn't have positive 'teaching'.
problems.fix: 'the foul odor of the ruler of this age's teaching' or 'the teaching that belongs to the ruler of this age'.

problems.quote: the Lord received anointing on his head
problems.why: 'Received anointing' is passive and ambiguous; reader may think of a literal ceremony rather than scriptural symbolism.
problems.fix: Render as 'the Lord was anointed on his head' or clarify the reference.

edits.old: the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age
edits.new: the foul odor of the ruler of this age's teaching

fixed: Changed 'the teaching of the ruler of this age' to 'the ruler of this age's teaching' to clarify that the teaching belongs to the ruler of this age, not that the ruler has a positive teaching.

Left 'the Lord received anointing on his head' unchanged: the Greek μύρον ἔλαβεν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος literally means 'the Lord received ointment on his head,' and the English accurately renders this without implying a literal ceremony.

problems.quote: the foul odor of the ruler of this age's teaching
problems.why: 'Ruler of this age' is Satan, but 'his teaching' is odd; usually 'ruler of this age' is person, not source of teaching.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age.'

edits.old: the foul odor of the ruler of this age's teaching
edits.new: the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age

fixed: The source reads δυσωδίαν τῆς διδασκαλίας τοῦ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, 'the stench of the teaching of the ruler of this age.' The English 'the foul odor of the ruler of this age's teaching' is ambiguous and could imply the ruler possesses teaching, but the genitive chain clearly modifies 'teaching' by 'of the ruler of this age.' Rephrased to 'the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age.'

polish.changed: Clarified the metaphor of breathing incorruption, made the knowledge of God explicitly identified as Jesus Christ, and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.

notes.quote: The Lord received ointment on his head for this reason: so that he might breathe incorruption upon the church.
notes.why: 'Breathe incorruption' reads like a literal gloss; the metaphor is unclear.
notes.fix: Rephrase: 'so that he might impart incorruption to the church.'

polish.changed: Clarified the opening reference by making the causal connection explicit, kept the anointing imagery consistent, and smoothed the rhetorical questions into natural modern English while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: The Lord received ointment on his head
notes.why: The reference is to Jesus's anointing (cf. Mark 14:3-9, John 12:1-8) but is presented without context, and the connection to 'breathing incorruption upon the church' is obscure.
notes.fix: Add a note identifying the anointing at Bethany and explaining the patristic association of anointing with incorruption.

polish.changed: Clarified the anointing metaphor by changing 'breathe incorruption upon' to 'breathe incorruption into,' making the image of imparting life to the church more natural in English while preserving every claim and quotation.

notes.quote: the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age
notes.why: 'Foul odor' for false teaching; metaphor from anointing contrast.
notes.fix: Retain but note: opposite of Christ's sweet anointing.

notes.why: 'Breathe upon' is awkward; likely means 'impart' or 'infuse' incorruption.
